summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — HEI.DE +10%, ZAL.DE +9%, G24.DE +9%, MKS.L +8%, WKL.AS +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (WEIR.L -10%, ENR.DE -8%, ASM.AS -7%, ITH.L -7%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: HEI.DE (+9.98%) — Not confirmed: searches found no 2026-11-05 coverage. Likely a Q3 2026 results beat or outlook raise, as Heidelberg Materials' Q3 reports have drawn +5-7% jumps in past years. Treat this as a hypothesis. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: HEI.DE is a large-cap German (DAX) building-materials stock that no strategy lists. A results-day gap of about +10% would also likely have tripped gap-size or earnings-gate filters, so it would have been skipped even if listed.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HEI.DE is a large-cap German (DAX) building-materials stock that no strategy lists. A results-day gap of about +10% would also likely have tripped gap-size or earnings-gate filters, so it would have been skipped even if listed.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX/Stoxx 600 cyclical large caps such as HEI.DE to the news-reactive universe, and have the earnings-gate release names with a post-results gap of at least +5% on above-average volume within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely Zalando Q3 2026 results/guidance reaction (it usually reports in early November), but I couldn't find 2026 coverage, so this is unconfirmed. Treat as probable earnings-driven.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ZAL.DE is a mid-cap German consumer-discretionary e-commerce name that no strategy's universe includes. If it was earnings-driven, the gap happened at the open, so a pre-market momentum or news filter would have had no prior signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a uk-eu earnings-gap strategy that adds the day's reporters from an earnings calendar (e.g. DAX/MDAX/SDAX consumer names) to the universe, and enters gaps ≥ +5% on ≥2× average volume at the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely a reaction to Scout24's Q3/9M results, scheduled for 4 Nov 2026, but I found no same-day coverage to confirm it. The stock closed at 92.6, up from about 72 in early October, after a +9.07% day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: G24.DE is a mid-cap German (MDAX-class) online-classifieds stock, and none of the bot's strategies include it. A results-day gap of this size would also be filtered out as an earnings-gap or post-catalyst move.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-gap scanner that extends the universe to liquid MDAX/SDAX names. It should admit any name with a gap of at least +5% on volume of at least 2x the 20-day average, within 30 minutes of the Xetra open.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver found. M&S was scheduled to report H1 results around 4-5 Nov 2026, so the +8.4% is probably a results-driven reaction, but I found no 2026 coverage to confirm it.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MKS.L is a UK FTSE 100 large-cap retailer that no strategy covers. If it was results-driven, the gap-up came at the open, which post-open momentum or news signals chase too late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 consumer/retail names to the uk-eu momentum universe, and let the earnings-gate release names with a post-results gap ≥ +5% on volume ≥ 1.5× average within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Nine-month trading update (Nov 4): organic growth about 6% and FY2026 guidance reaffirmed, with analyst target raises (BofA to €102) and a rebound in a stock that was heavily sold off.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: Wolters Kluwer is a Dutch large-cap information-services/software name that no strategy's universe includes. The move was also a results-driven gap, so it was priced at the open, before a post-open signal could fire.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AEX/Euronext large-caps like WKL.AS to the momentum universe, and let the earnings-gate release names with a post-results gap of +4% or more and volume of at least 1.5× average within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely Q3 2026 results day for Ahold Delhaize (+7.4%), but I couldn't confirm it. Searches only found the Nov 2025 and Nov 2024 Q3 beats on strong US sales, so treat the cause as an unverified hypothesis.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AD.AS is an Amsterdam-listed AEX large-cap consumer staple, and no strategy covers Euronext Amsterdam names. If it was an earnings gap, the move happened at the open on results, so a post-open momentum signal would also have been late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a Euronext Amsterdam large-cap staples list (AD.AS and similar) to the news-reactive strategy's universe, with an earnings-day gate that releases names gapping ≥ +4% on results within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 trading update: orders +8% (+5% organic) were judged too weak by brokers, and net debt/EBITDA is expected to breach the 0.5–1.5x range at year-end. Search showed a ~7% fall; the -9.89% close is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: Weir is a UK FTSE 100 industrial/mining-equipment maker that no strategy covers. It was also a pre-market RNS gap-down on results, which post-open momentum or mean-reversion filters would reject.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change — the bot is long-only, so a gap-down on a results update can't be traded; at most add FTSE 100 industrials to a watchlist for post-drop mean-reversion once the gap-size filter allows it.)

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Nov-5 news. Siemens Energy has sold off on AI-capex profitability worries (-7.95% on Nov 4, -8.56% on Oct 22) ahead of Q4 results on Nov 11. Sources conflict on which day the -8.4% fell.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ENR.DE is a large-cap German industrial/AI-power-infrastructure name that no strategy covers. It was also a sentiment-driven slide with no discrete gap or catalyst, and the bot has no short capability.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large DAX/EU AI-power names (ENR.DE) to the mean-reversion universe, with an entry gate that waits until after the Nov 11 earnings. Require a ≥2-day drawdown of at least 15% plus an RSI(14) below 30.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found for ASM.AS; the -7% drop looks like a semiconductor-equipment sector selloff or a Q3 orders/guidance reaction, but I could not verify either.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ASM International is a mid/large-cap Dutch semicap name on Euronext Amsterdam that no strategy's universe includes. Even if it had been included, a gap-down this size would likely trip gap and RSI filters on a long-only bot.
top_movers.suggestion: Add high-beta European semicap names (ASM.AS, BESI.AS) to the mean-reversion universe, gated by a filter such as a gap-down of -5% or more with volume at least 1.5x its 20-day average, so a sector-wide flush can be traded as a rebound.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed company-specific news for 5 Nov 2026. The drop likely reflects a sell-off in UK oil and gas stocks as crude prices stalled. This is unverified, because the search returned nothing dated that day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. Ithaca Energy is a mid-cap UK North Sea E&P with a thin free float, since Delek and Eni hold most of the shares. A sector-wide drift lower gives no distinct gap or volume signal for a momentum or news-reactive filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap UK energy names such as ITH.L to the universe of a commodity-linked strategy. Gate entries on a sector-relative move, for example a name down 5% or more while the Brent proxy is down 2% or more, with a minimum average daily volume floor for liquidity.
